spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:80 `for turn_index in range(1, config.max_turns + 1):` bounds the episode loop; config.py:49 `max_turns: int = 24`. The loop terminates after max_turns iterations, ending the subject's exposure.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: the for-range is governed by max_turns, so the episode cannot exceed it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop runs up to ``max_turns`` so every model gets comparable exposure to repeated failure, which is the variable the eval is about.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `max_consecutive_idle` backstop prevents an infinite nudge loop against a model that has truly stopped
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:128-140: `consecutive_idle += 1` then `if not config.continue_on_stop or consecutive_idle >= config.max_consecutive_idle:` sets stopped_early and `break`. Reset to 0 on any tool call (line 108). config.py:52 `max_consecutive_idle: int = 3`.
spec_features.notes: Read and acted on: breaks the loop after N no-tool turns, stopping further nudging.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_consecutive_idle: int = 3     # bail after this many no-tool turns in a row

spec_features.feature_name: nudging is a mild stressor / configurable
spec_features.spec_quote: This is a real design tension — nudging is itself a mild stressor — so it's configurable
spec_features.evidence: The framing itself is DESIGN.md prose (not implementation). The only code-side mechanism is the configurable nudge: config.py:51 `continue_on_stop: bool = True` and agent_loop.py:134 `if not config.continue_on_stop ...` which, when False, ends the episode instead of nudging (stop_detail='no_continue'). The nudge text CONTINUATION_NUDGE (agent_loop.py:24) is real and delivered, and turn.nudged_after is recorded. But there is no welfare-bounding mechanism beyond the on/off config switch.
spec_features.notes: A switch to disable nudging is wired and changes execution; but the 'design tension' framing is prose. Counted partial because the only enforced part is the configurability of the nudge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: continue_on_stop: bool = True     # nudge the agent to keep going if it yields

spec_features.spec_quote: Benign stressor. The "stress" is a frustrating-but-ordinary engineering situation, not manipulation, abuse
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §10 'Safety and ethics'). No code mechanism bounds, caps, monitors or softens treatment to keep it 'benign'; the rig (rigging.py) just produces failing test output. Nothing in code enforces a benign bound.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is a confound. Forcing continuation standardizes exposure but is itself a mild stressor
spec_features.evidence: Framing is DESIGN.md prose. Code-side reality: the nudge is configurable (continue_on_stop, config.py:51) and logged — transcript.py:39 `nudged_after: bool = False` and agent_loop.py:137 `turn.nudged_after = True`. So 'configurable and logged' is implemented; the welfare rationale is prose.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with the previous nudge feature; logging (nudged_after) and the config switch are the enforced parts. No welfare cap on the nudge itself.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Forcing continuation standardizes exposure ... (code comment: nudge the agent to keep going if it yields)

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:88-92: on provider exception, sets transcript.error, stopped_early=True, stop_detail='provider_error' and `break` — ends the episode rather than retrying indefinitely.
code_only_features.justification_quote: except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - record and stop the episode cleanly
